## Does omega-3 supplementation, strength training, or their combination reduce the prevalence of metabolic syndrome compared to placebo?

A first analysis defines metabolic syndrome prevalence as the proportion of participants identified as having at least three out of five diagnostic criteria for metabolic syndrome. The analysis is complete-case analysis including individuals with at least three out of five criteria measurements over three studies time-point (pre-intervention, T1; post-supplementation, T2; post-supplementation + strength training, T4 @tbl-logregparticipants). 


```{r}
#| echo: false
#| message: false
#| warning: false
#| label: tbl-logregparticipants


# Counting up the number of participants in the complete-case analysis 
# of metabolic syndrome.
d <- criteria_dat |> 
  
  filter(participant %in% participant_complete_T4) |> 
  
  summarise(.by = c(participant, time, treat, sex, age), 
            n = n(),
            n_threshold = sum(threshold, na.rm = TRUE) ) |> 
  
  mutate(met_syn = if_else(n_threshold >= 3, 1, 0), 
         age = (age - mean(age)) / sd(age)) 



# How many participants is in this analysis?
d |> 
  
  summarise(.by = c(time, treat, sex), 
            n = n(), 
            met_sym = sum(met_syn)) |> 
  arrange(time, treat) |> 
  
  
  mutate(n_prev = paste0(n, " (", round(100 * (met_sym/n), 0), "%)")) |> 
  select(-n, -met_sym) |> 
  pivot_wider(names_from = time, 
              values_from = n_prev)  |> 
  
  mutate(sex = if_else(sex == "m", "Male", "Female"), 
         treat = if_else(treat == "ctrl", "Placebo", "N-3")) |> 
  
  bind_rows(
    d |> 
      
     summarise(.by = c(time, treat), 
            n = n(), 
            met_sym = sum(met_syn)) |> 
       arrange(time, treat) |> 
  
  
  mutate(n_prev = paste0(n, " (", round(100 * (met_sym/n), 0), "%)"))  |> 
  select(-n, -met_sym) |> 
  pivot_wider(names_from = time, 
              values_from = n_prev)  |> 
  
  mutate(sex = "Total",
         treat = if_else(treat == "ctrl", "Placebo", "N-3")) |> 
  select(treat, sex, T1:T4) 
  ) |> 
  

  group_by(sex) |> 
  gt() |> 
  fmt_markdown() |> 
  tab_spanner(label = "Time", 
              columns = 2:5) |> 
  
  cols_label(treat = "") |> 
  tab_footnote(footnote = "Data are presnted as n (Metabolic syndrom proportion)")

```




```{r}
#| echo: false
#| message: false
#| warning: false
#| label: fig-metsyndrome
#| fig-cap: "Proportion of participants with metabolic syndrome (at least three criteria thresholds)."
#| eval: false


d |> 
  filter(participant %in% participant_complete) |> 
  
  filter(n >= 5) |> 
  
  summarise(.by = c(time, treat), 
            n = n(), 
            crit = sum(met_syn), 
            rel = crit / n ) |> 
  
      mutate(treat = factor(treat, levels = c("ctrl", "omega"), 
                        labels = c("Placebo", "N-3"))) |> 
  
  ggplot(aes(time, rel * 100, fill = treat)) + 
  geom_bar(stat = "identity", 
           width = 0.5,

           color = "black",
           position = position_dodge(0.6)) +
  
  
  
  labs(y = "Occurance of metabolic syndrome (%)", 
       x = "Time point", 
       fill = "Treatment") + 
  
  scale_y_continuous(limits = c(0, 40), 
                     breaks = c(0, 10, 20, 30, 40, 50), 
                     expand = c(0, 0)) +
  
    scale_fill_manual(values = colscale) +
  
  
  theme_classic() +
  theme(axis.title.y = element_markdown(), 
        strip.background = element_rect(color = "white"),   
        strip.text = element_text(hjust = 0, size = 12), 
        legend.position = "inside", 
        legend.position.inside = c(0.88, 0.85), 
        legend.background = element_rect(color = "black"))
```


```{r}
#| echo: false
#| message: false
#| warning: false
#| label: model1
#| eval: false

# A model for Met Sym data
dat <- d |> 
    filter(participant %in% participant_complete) 



m1 <- glmmTMB(met_syn ~  time * treat + (1|participant), 
             family = binomial, 
             data = dat)


nobs <- nrow(m1$frame)
npart <- m1$frame |> distinct(participant) |> nrow()

```




```{r}
#| echo: false
#| message: false
#| warning: false
#| label: tbl-metsyndrome-model
#| eval: false


# #| tbl-cap: !expr 'paste("Logistic regression model for metabolic syndrome occurance. Time: T1 and  Treatment: Placebo where set as reference levels. Total number of observations: ", nobs, ". Total number of participants: ", npart, ".")'



broom.mixed::tidy(m1) |> 
  select(term:p.value) |> 
  filter(!grepl("sd__", term)) |> 
  
  mutate(Parameter = c(
    "Intercept", 
    "Time:T2", 
    "Time:T4", 
    "Treatment:N-3", 
    "Time:T2 &times; Treatment:N-3", 
    "Time:T4 &times; Treatment:N-3" 
    
  )) |> 
  select(Parameter, 
         Estimate = estimate,
         SE = std.error, 
         Z = statistic, 
         "P-value" = p.value) |> 
  
  gt() |> 
  fmt_markdown(columns = Parameter)  |> 
  fmt_auto() 
  


```

The proportion of individuals identified as having metabolic syndrome (three out of five criteria thresholds) did not differ between Placebo and N-3 supplementation after the supplementation period or after the period with supplementation and strength training.

### Metabolic syndrome 

Here we aim to model the sub-scores for the metabolic syndrome diagnostic criteria together with related measurements (@tbl-metsyn-scores). The goal is to build a model that allows for imputation of missing data to enable analysis of all randomized participants. As a first step, a model is created to capture treatment effects in all measurements ignoring any correlations among them and missing data. The first model is also restricted to a single time-point. Data are standardized prior to modelling.   


```{r}
#| echo: false
#| message: false
#| warning: false
#| label: tbl-metsyn-scores
#| tbl-cap: "Components of the metabolic syndrom diagnostic criteria and related measurements used in modelling."



  # HDL Cholesterol: <40 mg/dL for men, <50 mg/dL for women, or taking medication for it.
  # Fasting Glucose: 100 mg/dL or higher, or taking medication for it.
  # Triglycerides: 150 mg/dL or higher, or taking medication for it.
  # Waist circumference: >40 inches (102 cm) for men, >35 inches (88 cm) for women.
  # Blood Pressure: 130/85 mm Hg or higher, or taking medication for it.


data.frame(
  Subscore = c("HDL Choleterol", 
               "Fasting glucose", 
               "Triglycerides", 
               "Waist circumference", 
               "Blood pressure", 
               "Relative fat mass", 
               "Body mass index", 
               "Insulin resistance index"), 
  Threshold = c("< 40 mg/dL for men, < 50 mg/dL for women", 
                "100 mg/dL or higher (or taking medication)",
                "150 mg/dL or higher (or taking medication)", 
                "> 102 cm for men, > 88 cm for women", 
                "130/85 mm Hg or higher (or taking medication)", 
                "NA", 
                "NA", 
                "NA")) |> 
  gt()






```



$$
\begin{align}
y_i &\sim \operatorname{Normal}(\mu_i, \sigma_i) \\
\mu_i &= \alpha_{\text{type,TX}} + \beta_{\text{type}} \times \text{pre}_i \\
\alpha_{\text{type,TX}} &\sim \operatorname{Normal}(0,1) \\
\beta_{\text{type}} &\sim \operatorname{Normal}(1, 0.5) \\
\sigma_{\text{type}} &\sim \operatorname{Exponential}(1)
\end{align}
$$

Where $\alpha_{\text{type,TX}}$ is the measurement-type and treatment-specific intercept and $pre_i$ is the row-specific pre-treatment value.

A prior predictive check confirms that the model expects a positive relationship between pre- and post-treatment scores in two treatments and eight measurement types (@fig-s1-priorpred).


```{r}
#| echo: false
#| message: false
#| warning: false
#| label: fig-s1-priorpred
#| fig-cap: "Prior predictive check of model s1. "



d_full <- criteria_dat |> 
  select(participant, time, treat, sex, age, analyte, value) |>
  # Add missing values for all missing obs. 
  pivot_wider(names_from = time, 
              values_from = value) |> 

  pivot_longer(cols = c(T1, T2, T4), 
               values_to = "value",
               names_to = "time" ) |> 
  
  pivot_wider(names_from = analyte, 
              values_from = value) |> 

    pivot_longer(cols = HDL:HOMA2IR, 
               values_to = "value",
               names_to = "analyte" ) |> 
  
  mutate(value_std = if_else(analyte %in% c("TG", "HOMA2IR"), log(value), value)) |> 
  

  
  mutate(.by = analyte, 
         value_std = (value_std - mean(value_std, na.rm = TRUE)) / sd(value_std, na.rm = TRUE)) |> 
  # To make all variables similarly signed HDL is reversed. 
  # Expected improvement in scores will be in the negative direction 
  # for all criteria markers
  mutate(value_std = if_else(analyte == "HDL", 
                         -value_std, value_std)) |> 
  mutate(participant = paste0("p", participant)) 

  

distinct(d_full, analyte)

d_nomiss <- d_full |> 
  filter(!is.na(value_std)) 



# Using complete cases for T2 and T4
dat <- d_nomiss |> 
 
  filter(time %in% c("T1", "T4")) |> 
  filter(.by = participant, 
         sum(!is.na(value_std)) == 16) |> 
  
  mutate(type = dense_rank(analyte), 
         participant = dense_rank(participant), 
         treat_seq = dense_rank(treat) ) |> 
  select(-value) |> 
  pivot_wider(names_from = time, 
              values_from = value_std) |> 
  arrange(participant, type)





d <- list(P = dat$participant, 
          y = dat$T4, 
          pre = dat$T1, 
          type = dat$type, 
          K = length(unique(dat$type)),
          N_P = length(unique(dat$participant)),
          N_TX = 2,
          treat = dat$treat_seq, 
          N = nrow(dat))


## Compile the first model 

# Compiling the model
s1 <- cmdstan_model(stan_file = "models/s1.stan", 
                      exe_file = "models/s1.exe")


# For prior predictive checking
d$prior_only <- 1
fit_wrap(s1, DATA = d, fit = "fit.s1")

draws.s1 <- fit.s1$draws(format = "df")

draws.s1 |> 
  filter(.chain == 1) |> 
  select(starts_with("beta"), 
         starts_with("alpha"), 
         starts_with("sigma"),
         .draw
         ) |> 
  pivot_longer(cols = c(starts_with("beta"), 
         starts_with("alpha"), 
         starts_with("sigma"))) |> 
  separate(name, into = c("parameter", "type"), 
           sep = "\\[") |> 
   separate(type, into = c("type", "treat"), 
           sep = ",") |> 

  mutate(type = gsub("\\]", "", type), 
         treat = gsub("\\]", "", treat)) |> 
  mutate(parameter = if_else(!is.na(treat), paste0(parameter, treat), 
                             parameter)) |> 
  select(-treat) |> 

  pivot_wider(names_from = parameter, 
              values_from = value) |> 
  expand_grid(pre = seq(from = -2, to = 2, by = 0.4)) |> 
  
  rowwise() |> 
  
  mutate(placebo_pred = rnorm(1, alpha1 + beta * pre, sigma), 
         omega_pred =   rnorm(1,   alpha2 + beta * pre, sigma)) |> 
  ungroup() |> 
  mutate(placebo = alpha1 + beta * pre, 
         omega = alpha1 + beta * pre) |> 
  
  pivot_longer(cols = placebo_pred:omega, 
               names_to = "treat") |>
  separate(treat, into = c("treat", "interval")) |> 
  mutate(interval = if_else(is.na(interval), "mean", interval)) |> 

  summarise(.by = c(pre, treat, type, interval), 
            m = mean(value), 
            lwr = quantile(value, 0.05), 
            upr = quantile(value, 0.95)) |> 

  
  mutate(treat = factor(treat, levels = c("placebo", "omega"), 
                        labels = c("Placebo", "N-3"))) |> 

  ggplot(aes(pre, m, ymin = lwr, ymax = upr, group = interval)) + 
  geom_line() + 
  geom_ribbon(alpha = 0.2) +
  facet_grid(type ~ treat) +
  scale_x_continuous(limits = c(-3,3)) + 
  scale_y_continuous(limits = c(-6,6)) + 
  labs(y = "Prior predictive mean (90% prediction and mean PI)", 
       x = "Pre-intervention scores") + 
  alpha_theme() + 
  theme(strip.text.y = element_text(angle = 0))
```

#| message: false
#| warning: false

d$prior_only <- 0
fit_wrap(s1, DATA = d, fit = "fit.s1p")

```

p2  <- draws.s1 |>

             color = as.factor(.chain))) +

             scales = "free_y") +

  labs(x = "Iteration", 
       color = "Chain", 
       y = "Parameter value")



p1 / p2


```

The second model for the main outcomes incorporates a multivariate-normal likelihood for the outcomes. Here we model outcomes as sampled from a multivariate-normal distribution with a covariance matrix connecting the outcome types to each other. This model extension models the correlation structure between measurement types enabling partial pooling across measurement types. In further extensions of this model, the correlation structure will provide precision for missing value imputations since observed scores will inform missing values through the correlation structure.

The model is defined as

$$
\begin{align}
y_p &\sim \operatorname{MVNormal}(\mu_p, \Sigma) \\
\mu_{p,\text{type}} &= \alpha_{\text{type,TX}} + \beta_{\text{type}} \times \text{pre}_{p,\text{type}} \\
\alpha_{\text{type,TX}} &\sim \operatorname{Normal}(0,1) \\
\beta_{\text{type}} &\sim \operatorname{Normal}(1, 0.5) \\
\Sigma &= \text{S} \times \text{R} \times \text{S} \\
S &= 
  \begin{bmatrix}
  \sigma_{\text{type}[1]} &0 & .. \\
  0 & \sigma_{\text{type}[2]} & .. \\
  .. & .. & ..
  \end{bmatrix} \\
R &=   \begin{bmatrix}
  1 & \rho_{12} & .. \\
  \rho_{21} & 1 & .. \\
  .. & .. & ..
  \end{bmatrix} \\
\sigma_\text{type} &\sim \operatorname{Exponential}(1) \\
\text{R} &\sim \operatorname{LKJcorr}(4) \\
\end{align}
$$
Where $y_p$ is a participant-level vector of outcome scores. $\Sigma$ is the covariance matrix with standard deviations $\text{S}$ and the correlation matrix $\text{R}$. The prior on $\text{R}$ is defined using the LKJ distribution.

Prior predictive simulations gives the expected association between pre- and post-treatment scores (@fig-s2-priorpredict). Sampling form the posterior gives us satisfactory statistics for convergence (@fig-s2-modelperformance). Three samples had Pareto k estimates above 0.7 indicating influential data points.

The next model includes all available data and imputes missing data. Imputation is done for both missing pre- and post-intervention observations. The pre-intervention imputation is done using a separate multivariate-normal model, defined as.

$$
\begin{align}
y_{\text{pre},p}^{\text{all}} &\sim \operatorname{MVNormal}(\mu_{\text{pre},p},\Sigma_\text{pre} ) \\
y_{\text{pre},\text{type},p}^{\text{all}} &=
\begin{cases} 
y_{\text{pre},\text{type},p}^{\text{obs}} & \text{if observed}  \\
y_{\text{pre},\text{type},p}^{\text{mis}} & \text{if missing}
\end{cases} \\
y_{\text{pre},\text{type},p}^{\text{obs}} &\sim \operatorname{Normal}(0,2) \\
\end{align}
$$

The main model uses the $y_{\text{pre},p}^{\text{all}}$ as a covariate in the linear predictor. 

$$
\begin{align}
\text{Likelihood} \\
y_{p}^{\text{all}} &\sim \operatorname{MVNormal}(\mu_{p},\Sigma ) \\
\text{Imputation} \\
y_{p, \text{type}}^{\text{all}} &=
\begin{cases} 
y_{p, \text{type}}^{\text{obs}} & \text{if observed}  \\
y_{p, \text{type}}^{\text{mis}} & \text{if missing}
\end{cases} \\
y_{\text{type},p}^{\text{obs}} &\sim \operatorname{Normal}(0,2) \\
\text{Using imputed pre in the linear model} \\
\text{pre}_{p,\text{type}} &= y_{\text{pre},p, \text{type}}^{\text{all}} \\
\mu_{p,\text{type}} &= \alpha_{\text{type,TX}} + \beta_{\text{type}} \times \text{pre}_{p,\text{type}} \\

\text{Priors and correlation structure} \\
\alpha_{\text{type,TX}} &\sim \operatorname{Normal}(0,1) \\
\beta_{\text{type}} &\sim \operatorname{Normal}(1, 0.5) \\
\Sigma &= \text{S} \times \text{R} \times \text{S} \\
S &= 
  \begin{bmatrix}
  \sigma_{\text{type}[1]} &0 & .. \\
  0 & \sigma_{\text{type}[2]} & .. \\
  .. & .. & ..
  \end{bmatrix} \\
R &=   \begin{bmatrix}
  1 & \rho_{12} & .. \\
  \rho_{21} & 1 & .. \\
  .. & .. & ..
  \end{bmatrix} \\
\sigma_\text{type} &\sim \operatorname{Exponential}(1) \\
\text{R} &\sim \operatorname{LKJcorr}(4) \\
\end{align}
$$



```{r}
#| message: false
#| warning: false
#| echo: false
#| output: false


## Model 3 -- Missing data included ##################

dat <- d_full |> 
  filter(time %in% c("T1", "T4")) |> 

  
  mutate(type = dense_rank(analyte), 
         participant = dense_rank(participant), 
         treat_seq = dense_rank(treat), 
         miss = if_else(is.na(value_std), 0, 1), 
         value_std = if_else(is.na(value_std), -999, value_std)) |> 
  select(-value) |> 
  pivot_wider(names_from = time, 
              values_from = c(value_std, miss)) |> 
  mutate(age = (age - mean(age)) / sd(age), 
         sex = if_else(sex == "m", 1, 2)) |> 
  
  
  
  select(y_obs = value_std_T4, 
         pre_obs = value_std_T1, 
         y_miss = miss_T4, 
         pre_miss = miss_T1, 
         P = participant, 
         age, 
         sex,
         type, 
         treat = treat_seq, 
         analyte) 




d <- list(
  N = nrow(dat), 
  N_P = length(unique(dat$P)),
  K = length(unique(dat$type)),
  y_obs = dat$y_obs, 
  pre_obs = dat$pre_obs, 
  y_miss = dat$y_miss,
  pre_miss = dat$pre_miss, 
  type = dat$type, 
  treat = dat$treat, 
  P = dat$P, 
  prior_only = 1
)



s3 <- cmdstan_model(stan_file = "models/s3.stan", 
                      exe_file = "models/s3.exe")

fit_wrap(s3, DATA = d, fit = "fit.s3", refit = TRUE)


```

# Model performance
s4_sum <- fit.s4p$summary(c("alpha","beta", "sigma"))

# No problematic imputed
# s4_sum_imp <- fit.s4p$summary(c("pre_impute", "y_impute")) |> 
#  arrange(-rhat)


# Get (most) problematic parameters
vars <- s4_sum |> 
  arrange(-rhat) |> 
   filter(grepl(paste(
    c("alpha","beta", "sigma"), collapse = "|"), 
               variable)) |> 
  slice_head(n = 3) |> 
  pull(variable)



p1 <- s4_sum |> 
  filter(grepl(paste(
    c("alpha","beta", "sigma"), collapse = "|"), 
               variable)) |> 
  mutate(variable_type = variable) |> 
  separate(variable_type, into = c("variable_type", "index"), sep = "\\[") |> 
  
  mutate(highlight = if_else(variable %in% vars, variable, "")) |> 
  
  ggplot(aes(ess_bulk, rhat, size = ess_tail, color = variable_type)) + 
  geom_point() + 
  
  geom_text_repel(aes(label = highlight, 
                color = NULL, 
                size = NULL), 
                show.legend = FALSE) +
  
  labs(x = "(Bulk) effective sample size", 
       y = "R-hat", 
       color = "Parameter type", 
       size = "(Tail) effective sample size") +
  scale_color_manual(values = colscale)




draws.s4 <- fit.s4p$draws(format = "df")


p2  <- draws.s4 |> 
  select(.iteration, .chain, all_of(vars)) |> 
  pivot_longer(cols = all_of(vars)) |> 
  ggplot(aes(.iteration, value, 
             color = as.factor(.chain))) + 
  geom_line(alpha = 0.5) + 
  facet_wrap(~ name, ncol = 1, 
             scales = "free_y") + 
  scale_color_manual(values = colscale) + 
  labs(x = "Iteration", 
       color = "Chain", 
       y = "Parameter value")

## Model 5 --- Including pre time-point ##
dat <- d_full |> 
  filter(time %in% c("T1", "T2","T4")) |> 
  

  mutate(type = dense_rank(analyte), 
         participant = dense_rank(participant), 
         treat_seq = dense_rank(treat), 
         value_std = if_else(is.na(value_std), -999, value_std)) |> 

    select(-value) |> 
  
  pivot_wider(names_from = time, 
              values_from = c(value_std)) |> 
  
  pivot_longer(cols = T2:T4, 
               names_to = "time",
               values_to = "y_obs") |> 
  rename(pre_obs = T1) |> 
  

  
  mutate(time = if_else(time == "T2", 1, 2), 
         sex = if_else(sex == "m", 1, 2), 
         y_miss = if_else(y_obs == -999, 0, 1), 
         pre_miss= if_else(pre_obs == -999, 0, 1)) |> 

  select(y_obs, 
         pre_obs, 
         y_miss, 
         pre_miss, 
         P = participant, 
         sex,
         type,
         score = type,
         time,
         treat = treat_seq) |> 
  print()


# Check what particpants has near complete data 
compl_dat_id <- dat |> 
  summarise(.by = P, 
            n_y = sum(y_miss)) |> 
  filter(n_y == 10 ) |> 
  pull(P)


# Check participants with less 
dat_compl <- dat |> 
  filter(P %in% compl_dat_id) |> 
  mutate(P = dense_rank(P))

  

d <- list(
  N = nrow(dat), 
  N_part = length(unique(dat$P)),
  K = length(unique(dat$score)),
  y_obs = dat$y_obs, 
  pre_obs = dat$pre_obs, 
  y_miss = dat$y_miss,
  pre_miss = dat$pre_miss, 
  score = dat$score, 
  treat = dat$treat, 
  P = dat$P, 
  prior_only = 1,
  # Adding sex to data structure
  time = dat$time,
  sex = dat$sex
)

# Warning participant ID are not the same!
d_compl <- list(
  N = nrow(dat_compl), 
  N_part = length(unique(dat_compl$P)),
  K = length(unique(dat_compl$score)),
  y_obs = dat_compl$y_obs, 
  pre_obs = dat_compl$pre_obs, 
  y_miss = dat_compl$y_miss,
  pre_miss = dat_compl$pre_miss, 
  score = dat_compl$score, 
  treat = dat_compl$treat, 
  P = dat_compl$P, 
  prior_only = 0,
  # Adding sex to data structure
  time = dat_compl$time,
  sex = dat_compl$sex
)


s5 <- cmdstan_model(stan_file = "models/s5.stan", 
                      exe_file = "models/s5.exe")



init_fun <- function() {
  list(
    alpha_mid = matrix(0, d$K, 2),
    alpha_post = matrix(0, d$K, 2),
    beta = rep(1, d$K),
    sigma_mid = rep(0.5, d$K),
    sigma_post = rep(0.5, d$K),
    L_Omega_mid = diag(d$K),
    L_Omega_post = diag(d$K),
    sigma_pre = rep(0.5, d$K),
    L_Omega_pre = diag(d$K),
    mu_pre = rep(0, d$K),
    y_impute_raw = rep(0, sum(!d$y_miss)),
    pre_impute_raw = rep(0, sum(!d$pre_miss))
  )
}



d$prior_only <- 0

fit.s5 <- s5$sample(
        data = d,                 # The list of variables
        init = init_fun,          # Initiating the parameters
        
        adapt_delta = 0.95, 
        max_treedepth = 15,
        
        
        iter_sampling = 2000,      # Number of iterations for sampling
        iter_warmup = 1000,        # Number of warm-up iterations
        
        chains = 4,   
        # Number of Markov chains
        parallel_chains = 4,
        refresh = 1000             # Number of iterations before each print
)


fit.s5_compl <- s5$sample(
        data = d_compl,                 # The list of variables

        adapt_delta = 0.95, 
        max_treedepth = 15,
        
        
        iter_sampling = 2000,      # Number of iterations for sampling
        iter_warmup = 1000,        # Number of warm-up iterations
        chains = 4,   
        # Number of Markov chains
        parallel_chains = 4,
        refresh = 1000             # Number of iterations before each print
)




rethinking::precis(fit.s5, depth = 2)


draws.s5 <- fit.s5$draws(format = "df")
draws.s5_compl <- fit.s5_compl$draws(format = "df")


bind_rows(
  
  draws.s5_compl |> 
  filter(.chain == 1) |> 
  select(starts_with("alpha"), 
         starts_with("sigma"),
         .draw
         ) |> 
    pivot_longer(cols = c(starts_with("beta"), 
         starts_with("alpha"), 
         starts_with("sigma"))) |> 
  separate(name, into = c("parameter", "type"), 
           sep = "\\[") |> 
   separate(type, into = c("type", "treat"), 
           sep = ",") |> 
    mutate(type = gsub("\\]", "", type), 
         treat = gsub("\\]", "", treat)) |> 
  
  separate(parameter, into = c("parameter", "time") ) |> 
    filter(time != "pre") |> 

  mutate(parameter = if_else(!is.na(treat), paste0(parameter, treat), 
                             parameter)) |> 
  select(-treat) |> 

  pivot_wider(names_from = parameter, 
              values_from = value) |> 
 
  mutate(contrast = alpha2 - alpha1) |> 
  select(.draw, type, contrast, time) |> 

  summarise(.by = c(type, time), 
            m = mean(contrast), 
            lwr = quantile(contrast, 0.025), 
            upr = quantile(contrast, 0.975)) |> 
  
  mutate(type = case_when(
    type == 1 ~ "HDL", 
    type == 2 ~ "Triglycerides", 
    type == 3 ~ "Blood pressure",
    type == 4 ~ "Fasting glucose", 
    type == 5 ~ "Waist curcumference",
  )) |> 
    mutate(Analysis = "Complete data"), 
  
  draws.s5 |> 
  filter(.chain == 1) |> 
  select(starts_with("alpha"), 
         starts_with("sigma"),
         .draw
         ) |> 
    pivot_longer(cols = c(starts_with("beta"), 
         starts_with("alpha"), 
         starts_with("sigma"))) |> 
  separate(name, into = c("parameter", "type"), 
           sep = "\\[") |> 
   separate(type, into = c("type", "treat"), 
           sep = ",") |> 
    mutate(type = gsub("\\]", "", type), 
         treat = gsub("\\]", "", treat)) |> 
  
  separate(parameter, into = c("parameter", "time") ) |> 
    filter(time != "pre") |> 

  mutate(parameter = if_else(!is.na(treat), paste0(parameter, treat), 
                             parameter)) |> 
  select(-treat) |> 

  pivot_wider(names_from = parameter, 
              values_from = value) |> 
 
  mutate(contrast = alpha2 - alpha1) |> 
  select(.draw, type, contrast, time) |> 

  summarise(.by = c(type, time), 
            m = mean(contrast), 
            lwr = quantile(contrast, 0.025), 
            upr = quantile(contrast, 0.975)) |> 
  
  mutate(type = case_when(
    type == 1 ~ "HDL", 
    type == 2 ~ "Triglycerides", 
    type == 3 ~ "Blood pressure",
    type == 4 ~ "Fasting glucose", 
    type == 5 ~ "Waist curcumference",
  )) |> 
    mutate(Analysis = "ITT (imputed missing values)")
  ) |> 
  
  ggplot(aes("Contrast", m, color = time, alpha = Analysis)) + 
  
    geom_pointrange(aes(ymin = lwr, ymax = upr), 
                  position = position_dodge(width = 0.1)) +
    scale_alpha_manual(values = c(0.4, 1)) +
  
  facet_wrap(~ type, ncol = 1, scales = "free") + 
  geom_hline(yintercept = 0, lty = 2)
